body: In https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/16315 we introduced support for `.bst` styles for LibreOffice. Currently, one can import multiple of those file with the same name: which can be confusing (regardless of whether they are actually the same style or different). "name" here is just the `.bst` filename with the extension stripped off, as these files do not specify a separate "name" field like CSL. In CSL Styles, we don't allow the import of two files with the same name. We show a dialog that such a style already exists. Goal is to have the same guard for the `.bst` tab. **This no-duplication mechanism should take into account both internal (default) and externally added styles in the list.** Note: Please explore the CSL code, warning messages etc properly before attempting this. Refer to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15463 for more hints.
title: Disallow importing multiple `.bst` files with the same filename

body: This is a tracking issue for lower priority bugs related to our BST integration (both Entry Preview Viewer as well as LibreOffice). These are hard to solve and are not "very" commonly used, so please prefer taking up other items in JabRef of higher priority. --- We already had BST rendering in our Entry Preview, and in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/16315 we introduced LibreOffice bibliography generation for them. The former uses BST VM + a rich HTML text renderer to preview, the latter uses BST VM + Pandoc + Manual Formatting to make the bibliography items compatible with LibreOffice. We currently have full support for standard and most commonly used APA, IEEETran, abbrv, etc. (in both preview viewer as well as LO), but more complex styles often fail. ## Known issues 1. https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/16326 - styles like these cannot be imported (VM limitation) 2. https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/16330 (some formatting like smallcaps as present in jfm cannot be rendered in preview, but works in LO). 3. Some more complex styles like [achemso.bst](https://github.com/AlbertDeFusco/texmf/blob/master/bibtex/bst/jpc/achemso.bst) does not render a preview at all (check event logs for details of where it fails) and also fails to generate LO bibliography. 4. Some complex styles like [amsalpha.bst](https://mirror.niser.ac.in/ctan/macros/latex/required/amscls/amsalpha.bst) don't render "properly" in the preview as it does an `ams.org` url call somewhere (as visible in the preview) but works alright with LO: 5. Some other complex styles like [apacite.bst](https://github.com/open-source-uc/latex-template-msc/blob/master/apacite.bst) don't render propely in preview with some weird braces and repetitions: and also don't render properly in LO: Below is a complexity chart for styles: (ignore the case of `alpha` - we support it fully as well as far as LO bibliography and previews go. We just don't support the citation format which has superscripts currently, and have no plans to support it either. Users can manually change the citation text and format them if they want, or use more automated workarounds like a matching CSL style, cite the items, and use BST to generate the bibliography instead).
title: Known issues with BST styles

body:
Currently, we let users interact with all LibreOffice related preferences in the "Settings" of the LibreOffice Integration panel.

After https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/16315 and also upcoming from https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/16349, it can be established that OO/LO integration now has a lot of preferences.

Maybe they deserve their own dedicated tab in File -> Preferences?

With a lighter number of preferences, our current OCR feature has its own preference tab (see https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15990).
This allows the OCR user to easily visualize the selected `ocrmypdf` path.

In LO, we have a `pandoc` path which can similarly be auto-detected or set manually. User should either get a notification informing them of the path selected, so that they can verify that they didn't make a mistake, or this full migration of preferences UI into a tab should be done so that they can always see the paths (like OCR).
title: (Idea) Move Open Office Preferences to a dedicated Preference tab

body: Currently in CSL Styles of the LibreOffice Integration, if not already present, a space is always added after the running text before the citation that is inserted. This can be frustrating to manually remove, especially in footnote-friendly styles like Nature where the citation has to be like this1 and not this 1 We already have a preference for "add space after" in the LO integration settings - goal is to make "insert space before" tweakable as well. The defaults should be insert space before - true, insert space after - true.
title: Make "Add space before citation" a preference

### JabRef version

Latest development branch build (please note build date below)

### Operating system

Other (please describe below)

### Details on version and operating system

WSL Ubuntu (Microsoft Windows 11 - Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS - Architecture: x86_64, WSL version: 2.7.10.0)

### Checked with the [latest development build](https://builds.jabref.org/main/) (copy version output from About dialog)

- [x] I made a backup of my libraries before testing the latest development version.
- [x] I have tested the latest development version and the problem persists

### Steps to reproduce the behaviour

1. Clone JabRef and initialize its submodules:

   ```
   git clone https://github.com/JabRef/jabref.git
   cd jabref
   git submodule update --init --recursive
   ```

2. Verify that JDK 25 or newer is active:

   ```
   java -version
   ./gradlew --version
   ```

3. Build JabRef:

   ```
   ./gradlew --stop
   ./gradlew clean :jabgui:compileJava :jablib:jar
   ```

4. Confirm that the build succeeds.

5. Launch JabRef using the development run task:

   ```
   ./gradlew :jabgui:run
   ```

### Appendix

<details>

Launching JabRef from source with the Gradle `:jabgui:run` task fails because the runtime does not contain or resolve the platform-specific embedded PostgreSQL binary module.

The project compiles successfully, and the failure occurs only when the application starts.

This is separate from the packaged-runtime problem fixed in #16323. That pull request configures the embedded PostgreSQL module for target-specific `jpackage` tasks and the generated packaged launcher. The ordinary Gradle `run` task does not use the generated `JabRef.cfg` and does not receive the equivalent host-specific module configuration.

JabRef fails during startup:

```
ERROR: No postgres binaries found, you need to add an appropriate maven dependency that meets the following parameters - system: 'Linux', architecture: 'x86_64'
ERROR: Could not launch JabRef: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Missing embedded postgres binaries
```

<summary>Log File</summary>

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Missing embedded postgres binaries
    at embedded.postgres@2.2.2/io.zonky.test.db.postgres.embedded.DefaultPostgresBinaryResolver.getPgBinary(DefaultPostgresBinaryResolver.java:81)
    at embedded.postgres@2.2.2/io.zonky.test.db.postgres.embedded.EmbeddedPostgres.prepareBinaries(EmbeddedPostgres.java:816)
    at embedded.postgres@2.2.2/io.zonky.test.db.postgres.embedded.EmbeddedPostgres.<init>(EmbeddedPostgres.java:135)
    at embedded.postgres@2.2.2/io.zonky.test.db.postgres.embedded.EmbeddedPostgres$Builder.start(EmbeddedPostgres.java:612)
    at org.jabref.jablib/org.jabref.logic.search.sqlbased.PostgresServer.<init>(PostgresServer.java:30)
    at org.jabref/org.jabref.Launcher.main(Launcher.java:96)
```

Gradle consequently reports:

```
> Task :jabgui:run FAILED

Execution failed for task ':jabgui:run'.
> Process finished with non-zero exit value 1
```
</details>

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `./gradlew :jabgui:run` launches successfully on Linux x86_64.
- [x] The corresponding host-specific binary works on Linux ARM64, macOS Intel, macOS ARM64, and Windows x86_64.
- [x] The `run` JVM resolves the selected embedded PostgreSQL module.
- [x] The embedded PostgreSQL server starts without `Missing embedded postgres binaries`.
- [x] Target-specific `jpackage` configurations continue to contain only the binary for their target platform.
- [x] Cross-platform package sizes do not increase by including binaries for unrelated platforms.

## Related issues and pull requests

- #16317
- #16323
- #16156
title: Gradle `:jabgui:run` fails because the host-specific embedded PostgreSQL binary module is missing

Thanks!
-->

**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**
When importing references through the browser extension, users can select "Download referenced PDF" in the import window that pops up. JabRef doesn't remember this selection*, so users have to repeat the step each time if they want a non-default option.

*Needs to be verified.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
JabRef should remember the user selection, even if it is not the default.

**Additional context**
There is also an option to automatically download referenced PDFs in Preferences > Web search. The web search download preference is not the same as the extension-import option and the two settings are not synchronized. @koppor proposes to treat extension-import option as a "preference" as represented in the architecture, but _not_ to expose it in the Preferences window (only show the option in the extension-import window).
title: Import from browser should remember user selection to download PDF

> @geritwagner Looks good to me overall, can you comment on the qodo comment? Is that a valid concern?

I believe runtime is a valid concern in the deduplication procedure. In my view, fully separating duplicate search from duplicate resolution should be preferred (see #15190). Once this is implemented, the **cancel** option in duplicate resolution should no longer affect the runtime of duplicate search. More broadly, a practical solution to the O(n²) runtime issue would be to introduce a blocking stage (see [1](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abi8021)).

_Originally posted by @geritwagner in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/16234#issuecomment-4989508883_
title: Duplicate resolution is O(n^2)

<!-- Please use the GitHub issue tracker only for bug reports and smaller suggestions for improvements. Requests for completely new features, questions and general feedback is now handled at https://discourse.jabref.org. Thanks! -->

**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**

On macOS, the outer corner radius of the main JabRef window appears visually inconsistent with standard native macOS applications. The window corners look slightly different from apps such as Finder, Preview, Notes, etc., which makes JabRef feel less native on macOS.

This is a small visual polish issue, but it is quite noticeable for users who are sensitive to platform consistency.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

The main JabRef window should match the standard macOS window shape as closely as possible, including the native corner radius and clipping behavior.

This may not be fixable through regular JavaFX CSS alone, since the outer window shape is likely controlled by the macOS/JavaFX native window layer rather than by controls inside the scene. A macOS-specific window styling adjustment, if feasible, might be a better approach than globally changing CSS border radii.

**Additional context**

I do not have a proposed patch yet. I am opening this issue to ask whether the maintainers would consider improving the native macOS window appearance, or whether this is a limitation of JavaFX on macOS.
title: Improve macOS window corner radius to better match native apps

I cloned `main` and counted the `l10n/JabRef_*.properties` files against `JabRef_en.properties` (2,846 keys, 25 languages). The top languages are in great shape — French 97%, Italian 95%, German 86% — but there's a long tail that's barely off the ground: Persian 2%, Ukrainian 2%, Arabic 4%, Danish 13%, Vietnamese 14%, Portuguese 24%, Swedish 29%.

I know translations go through Crowdin, so this isn't about replacing that. I maintain Bisq's localization tooling ([localize-pipeline](https://github.com/bisq-network/localize-pipeline)), which can draft the missing keys for a language so a native speaker has something to correct instead of a blank file. It keeps the `{0}` placeholders intact and can run on a local model. The output would still go through your normal review.

Is the long tail something you'd want to move on, and would AI-seeded drafts (still native-reviewed) fit how JabRef works — or not the direction you'd take? Fine either way.

cc @koppor

body:
**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**

JabRef offers library synchronization via:
- Shared SQL database
- Git

These only offer synchronization and collaborative abilities with the bib file itself, and not for files linked to each reference i.e. Linked Files. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

WebDAV is a file sharing protocol that can allow you to share files via HTTP. We can add native WebDAV support to JabRef allowing users to automatically sync Linked files. 
My idea for how this feature would work is something like the following:

1.) User setups a WebDAV server and connects to the server from JabRef
2.) Each entry can have it's own folder in the WebDAV server with the folder name being the citation key (maybe we can use something else here, I'll have to think about alternatives). All linked files of an entry is pushed to the corresponding folder. 
3.) Users can share a single WebDAV server for their shared library and also ensure linked files are shared. 

Sync will have to be handled with care to prevent unintentional overwrites and to handle conflicts. 

**Additional context**

- Sardine library: https://github.com/lookfirst/sardine can be used as the WebDAV client
- Related community discussion forum post: https://discourse.jabref.org/t/webdav-support-for-jabref/1316
title: Add Linked File Sync support with WebDAV

body:
After https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15798 is merged, we should aim to decrease the amount of CSS variables. 

Beside less CSS code, the UI will look more unified.
From my experience, many contributors added more and more styleClasses just for some padding. They now should use the common styleClasses (we should tell them in the PR review as well).

This has multiple advantages:

- Now, we can directly see that this is a header with a bigger font size and padding on top.
Before, we need to lookup sectionHeader in CSS.
- Now everything that is styled uses the same set of styles. So it should be more consistent. What is one header has a padding of 9, another one has 11, another has 10, another has 8? While we can still have very different paddings with this change, it is now much harder to use completely different values as we provide a fixed amount (and we should decrease that - in my apps, I usually only use a padding of 2,4, rarely 8) and that works pefectly fine.
- Last one: We now use em everywhere and there is no more px and new contributions should reuse that styles, so they can not make this wrong and add another new styleClass, as example subHeader, use a different font size and lets say 6px padding.
title: Decrease the amount of CSS variables

## Syntax highlighting for the source tab: incubator CodeArea + veneer

### Background

JabRef's source tab currently uses RichTextFX (`org.fxmisc.richtext`) for its `CodeArea`.
Since JavaFX 24, the JDK ships an incubator module `jfx.incubator.richtext` that contains its
own `CodeArea` with a `SyntaxDecorator` hook — JabRef already uses this module for the entry
preview (see JabRef/jabref#16145). Building on it for the source tab would let us retire the
RichTextFX dependency, continuing the dependency reduction started with the removal of
`javafx.web`.

For the highlighting itself, [veneer](https://github.com/kusoroadeolu/veneer) (MIT, Java 21+)
is a small syntax-highlighting library with **BibTeX support** built on ANTLR (thanks to @timurturbil). Its current
output format is ANSI-colored strings for terminals. For a GUI that is a lossy detour: veneer
has real tokens internally and flattens them to ANSI; the GUI would have to parse the escape
codes back into style runs. The better interface is a structured one.

### Action points   

1. **Upstream contribution to veneer**: propose (issue, then PR) a structured output API next
 to the ANSI printer — e.g. a sink/callback that emits `(token text, token type/style)`
 spans. The ANSI printer then becomes one implementation of that sink.
2. **Quick win, independent of the GUI**: colored BibTeX output in `jabkit` using veneer's
 ANSI output as-is. Terminals are exactly what ANSI is for; no parsing needed.
3. **Prototype the source tab** on the incubator `CodeArea`: implement a `SyntaxDecorator`
 that feeds veneer's BibTeX tokens (via the new structured API) into `RichParagraph` styles.
4. **Theming**: map the highlighting styles to JabRef's palette with looked-up colors. Note:
 Modena styles the incubator controls from `-fx-accent`, which JabRef deliberately sets to
 red as an "unthemed control" canary — new selectors must be added to `jabref-theme.css`
 (see the `.rich-text-area` section there for the pattern).
5. **Build plumbing**: follow `docs/code-howtos/dependency-management.md` — version pin in
 `versions/build.gradle.kts`, module mapping in `gradle/modules.properties` if needed, and
 platform-variant handling for JavaFX artifacts is already in place for
 `jfx-incubator-richtext`.

### Caveats

- `jfx.incubator.richtext` is an incubator module: the API may change with any JavaFX release.
JabRef has accepted this for the entry preview; the source tab would ride the same upgrades.
- veneer is a young project (single maintainer). For an optional highlighting feature that is
acceptable; the structured-API contribution also benefits the project directly.
title: Add BibTeX syntax highlighting

### Steps to reproduce the behaviour

3. Insert e1 into db1 and e2 into db2

BibDatabase db1 = new BibDatabase();

db2.insertEntry(e2);

db1 and db2 should be completely independent. Inserting e2 into db2
should have no effect on db1. db1.getEntries().contains(e2) should
return false.

inserted into db2. This is likely caused by the BibEntry equals()/hashCode()
bug — since all empty BibEntry objects share sharedId: -1 by default,

likely resolve this issue as well. Please refer to the related issue filed

body: ### JabRef version 5.15 (latest release) ### Operating system macOS ### Details on version and operating system macOS 26.3.1 (Apple Silicon M5) / JabRef 5.15 (2024-07-10-1eb3493) / Java 21.0.2 / JavaFX 22.0.1+7 ### Checked with the [latest development build](https://builds.jabref.org/main/) (copy version output from About dialog) - [x] I made a backup of my libraries before testing the latest development version. - [x] I have tested the latest development version and the problem persists ### Steps to reproduce the behaviour 1. Set up JabRef with shared PostgreSQL database mode. 2. Connect JabRef to the shared database successfully. 3. Run this SQL directly on the PostgreSQL database: INSERT INTO jabref."ENTRY" ("SHARED_ID", "TYPE", "VERSION") VALUES (9999, '', 1); 4. Open JabRef and look at your library - the entry does not appear anywhere in the UI. 5. Query the database directly: SELECT * FROM jabref."ENTRY" WHERE "TYPE" = '' OR "TYPE" IS NULL; 6. The entry exists in the database but is completely invisible in JabRef UI. Expected result: The database should reject the insert with a constraint violation error because every entry must have a valid type, such as Article, Book, or Conference. Actual result: Insert succeeds silently. Entry becomes a ghost entry that exists in database permanently, but JabRef cannot see or delete it. JabRef UI showed 100 entries, but the database had 102 entries total. Root cause: The TYPE column in jabref.ENTRY table has no NOT NULL or CHECK constraint in the schema, which is why the database accepts empty type values. ### Appendix The following screenshots are attached as evidence: 1. Ghost entry - SHARED_ID 8101 exists in the database with completely empty TYPE column. 2. Database count shows 102 entries, but JabRef UI only displays 100 entries - 2 ghost entries exist 3. JabRef official schema documentation showing the ENTRY table TYPE column defined as just 'varchar' with no NOT NULL constraint.
title: Shared PostgreSQL database schema missing NOT NULL constraint on ENTRY TYPE column allows ghost entries.

body:
## What?
JabRef allows users to create search groups using complex expressions. However, there is currently no way to understand why a given entry matches or does not match a search group.

## Why?
This makes debugging search expressions difficult, especially for complex conditions. Users are left guessing why an entry is included or excluded from a group, with no feedback from the application.

No equivalent feature currently exists in JabRef.

## Proposed Solution
When a user selects an entry and a search group, JabRef should display a breakdown of how each part of the search expression was evaluated against that entry.

For example, given the expression:
groups!=one AND file!=.pdf AND NOT groups=two

The explanation would show:

groups!=one     → false
file!=.pdf      → false
NOT groups=two  → true

This could be displayed as a tooltip on the group, or as a small panel in the entry editor when a search group is selected.
title: Match Explanation for Search Groups

body: This is the last bit (follow up) for the Theme Overhaul: - https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15545 - https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15573 - https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15579 Part of the #16043 Adding "First Class Theme Support" means that, as a user, you can still choose a theme (as you do now), but you can also select a separate color scheme for it. The color scheme is independent of the theme. Currently, you can provide a custom theme using CSS, but it isn't aware of color schemes. With this proposal, custom themes can support color schemes. It will also make it easy to add new themes (for example, another CSS theme like Primer) without code changes - only the CSS, theme name and the color variable mapping need to be done. This also aims to fix outstanding issues, like: - https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/15585 - In particular: We can merge Light/Dark Theme in https://github.com/JabRef/themes.jabref.org to one style. Makes housekeeping easier as well - Docs in: https://devdocs.jabref.org/architecture-and-components.html#theming
title: First Class Theme Support

We have bibliographic metadata that is created by users of JabRef, not the original author of the entry. We need to store this information somewhere.

So far, one option is/was to cache some information and not store it in the .bib file. This means, we lack persistence. Another option has been to utilize the comment-user field, such as in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15316. We also already make use of some custom bibtex fields that can be found in the General tab. (Sometimes I wonder, if we should rename that tab to JabRef fields or something like that, but that's a different issue).

Example for data that might be worthy of deserving their own field(s):

- [ ] references extracted from pdf files, such as references cited in and references cited by (can be found in Citations tab). Possible bibtex fields are described in https://docs.jabref.org/advanced/entryeditor/entrylinks. E.g. `cited` or `related`
- [ ] entries from related articles tab
- [ ] AI summarizations
- [ ] AI chat



When it comes to question if we should make a difference between user generated data and original "official" data created by the authors of the metadata item, I am in favor of doing so, for the following reason: If the field can be spelled without an abbreviation, then don't abbreviate it. Computers can easily shorten words, but not the other way. Computers can easily strip information from something, but adding new information requires work. Either compute or manual work. This follows the philosophy of the [OpenStreetMap project with regard to abbreviations](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Abbreviations): "If the [name](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Names) can be spelled without an abbreviation, then don't abbreviate it. Computers can easily shorten words, but not the other way (St. could be Street or Saint)."

Having an "user-mode" vs. an "author-mode" might be something worth exploring.

This is just a rough idea and would require a proper [ADR](https://devdocs.jabref.org/decisions/), if somebody wants to work on this. We already have two for AI related fields that opted to NOT store data in a bibtex field: https://devdocs.jabref.org/decisions/0032-store-chats-in-local-user-folder.html and https://devdocs.jabref.org/decisions/0033-store-chats-in-mvstore.html
title: New (custom) bibtex fields

# Drag-and-drop of library files (`.ris`, `.bib`, …) should trigger import dialog instead of linking as file

## Description

When dragging a library file (e.g., `.ris`, `.bib`) from a file manager onto JabRef, the file is treated as a regular file drop: a single entry is created with the library file attached as a linked file. This is unexpected — a user would naturally expect JabRef to recognize the file as a bibliography and offer to import its entries.

The expected behavior should be consistent with how `.bib` files are already handled on drag-and-drop, and should extend to all supported library formats.

### Expected behavior

JabRef detects that the dropped file is a library/bibliography file (by extension and/or content sniffing) and triggers the import workflow:

- **Drop on entry table:** Parse the file and open the "Select the entries to be imported" dialog, allowing the user to import entries into the current library (currently already works for `.bib` files).
- **Drop on library tab bar:** Open the file as a new library (currently: drop is not allowed on the tab bar).

### Current behavior

- **Drop on entry table:** A new entry is created with the dropped file set as a linked file. The file's bibliographic content is ignored.
- **Drop on library tab bar:** Drop is not allowed.

The only way to import is via **File → Import**, which disrupts workflow for users who habitually use drag-and-drop.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a `.ris` file (or other supported library format) on disk
2. Drag the file from the file manager onto the entry table in JabRef
3. Observe: a single new entry is created, with the `.ris` file linked as a file attachment
4. Expected: the import dialog ("Select the entries to be imported") opens

## Proposal

- When a file is dropped onto JabRef, check whether its extension matches a known library/bibliography format (`.ris`, `.enl`, `.xml` (EndNote/MODS/…),  etc.). 
- check for each importer if supported import format
- first hit: import

**Please check existing import functionality of JabRef** -- most porbably, coe fixing this just adds some lines of code.


---

You can get a `RIS` with multiple (!) entries by exporting to RIS https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-demonstration-libraries/blob/main/chocolate/Chocolate.bib https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-demonstration-libraries/blob/main/chocolate/Chocolate.bib

You can also have an AI generating it for you, but please **double check** correctness if you use real entries. You can also generat a RIS with two entries having artifical data (e.g., "author1" etc) to avoid checking two things.

## Pre-requisites
1. Context about [JabRef's **LibreOffice integration**](https://docs.jabref.org/cite/openofficeintegration)
2. Refer to [this blog article](https://blog.jabref.org/2024/08/26/GSoC-CSL/#getting-started) for an introduction to how [CSL styles](https://citationstyles.org/) are used with JabRef's LibreOffice integration.
3. Go through https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15369

---

## Problem Statement

Quoting from https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15369#issue-4099450218
> A more robust solution would be to embed the in-text nature in the CSL reference mark itself (like we do in JStyles), and when parsing the existing reference marks from the doc, use that piece of data to set whether inTextUsed is true, as otherwise there would be no way to retain the correct information if JabRef is restarted after using in-text citations - and thus generating bibliography would still refresh and overwrite them to normal citations.
Current workaround to that (if in-text citations were used and JabRef was restarted and now bibliography is to be generated without inserting another citation) is to insert another in-text citation and remove it to refresh the internal state. Similarly, if in-text citations were used and JabRef is restarted, and now the user wants to change the citation type to normal citations, they have to manually refresh the nature (to in-text and back to normal by inserting citations of respective styles once, and removing them).

This would involve two parts - 
1. Redesigning and re-implementing the reference mark format
2. Re-implementing the parsing logic and wiring the in-text related data with the existing related boolean variables (See changes in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15369 for more information).

This refs the GSoC project of cross compatible reference marks (https://github.com/JabRef/GSoC/blob/main/_posts/2025-12-26-libreoffice.md)
This can be solved within the project, or independently.

**Additional context**
See how JStyle embeds style type information:
https://devdocs.jabref.org/code-howtos/openoffice/overview.html#what-is-stored-in-a-document-jabref52
> Format: "JR_cite{number}_{type}_{citationKeys}", where
{number} is either empty or an unsigned integer (it can be zero) to make the name unique
**{type} is 1, 2, or 3 for parenthesized, in-text and invisible**
{citationKeys} contains the comma-separated list of citation keys
Examples:
JR_cite_1_Smith2000 (empty number part, parenthesized, single citation)
JR_cite0_2_Smith2000,Jones2001 (number part is 0, in-text, two citations)
JR_cite1_3_Smith2000,Jones2001 (number part is 1, invisible, two citations)
title: Enrich CSL Reference mark format with citation type information

body: JabRef can make better use of space in the library tab. It can show the number of entries in the library. This behavior is very common, similar to how GitHub shows the number of issues or pull requests in its tabs. The tab should display the total number of entries in the library. If the user selects specific entries, it should instead show the number of selected entries. **Describe the solution you'd like** A new tab design should be implemented for better UI and UX. It should display: 1. A document icon on the right side and a different icon for each library type - If mode == BibTeX → show the BibTeX icon [like badge BTX] - If mode == BibLaTeX → show the BibLaTeX icon [like badge BLX] 2. The total number of entries on the left side of close icon. [If the **Groups** sidebar is open, it should be turned off.] 3. Users can set custom icons for their libraries, for example, a Math library, a Chemistry library, a Java library, and more. 4. Like every feature, it should be toggleable from Preferences. **What impact will it have?** 1. Better context awareness. 2. Faster workflow Seeing the number of selected entries directly in the tab helps users quickly confirm operations such as exporting, deleting, or editing multiple references. 3. Alignment with modern UI patterns. 4. Improved visual organisation by having custom icons for a library. **If the [status bar](https://github.com/issues/created?issue=JabRef%7Cjabref%7C15245) feature request gets approved, many of the things will be included there, but things like custom icons will still be used.**
title: Better tab design

body:
Currently, users have to navigate through **Library menu**  **> Library Properties** to find basic metadata like file paths, library encoding, library mode and more.

JabRef should have a status bar at the bottom which should show:

1. Path Information 
2. Cursor Position [Row:Column]
3. Git Branch
4. Read-Only Toggle [Can be another feature]
5. Background Task Status [Show loading
6. Library Metadata
7. Show the total number of entries selected

**Describe the solution you'd like**

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db1d75c3-4f01-425a-a3ec-426ec90743e9)

Just like IntelliJ IDEA and VS Code have, JabRef can have it too as well to

- Reduce cognitive load
- Improve conttext awareness

This is a "Quality of life" feature that all modern software have.

**Additions**
To ensure the UI remains clean and adaptable to different workflows, I suggest the following:

- Users should have the option on what should be shown in the status bar.
- Users should be able to enable or disable the entire status bar via the Preferences menu.
title: Implement a modern status bar

body:
## What?
Currently, the 'Find Duplicates' command would scan the library for duplicates and prompt users to resolve them immediately. This is overwhelming and not needed.

## Why?
The current duplicate resolution flow is similar to that of Git merge conflict resolution. In Git, when you attempt a merge and encounter conflicts, the repository enters a conflicted state. You must resolve all conflicts and complete the merge or abort it entirely. Leaving conflicts unresolved risks breaking the codebase.

But unlike code conflicts, having duplicates in your library does not necessarily render it invalid; it is merely an undesirable state. It does not require immediate action. Thus, users should be given the freedom to resolve duplicates and select which duplicates to resolve at their own time.

It will simplify code as well.

## How?
- `FindDuplicates` should be split into  commands: `FindDuplicates` and `ResolveDuplicates`
- `FindDuplicates` would search for duplicates in the current library and add them to a special 'Duplicates' group.
- `ResolveDuplicates` would loop through entries in the 'Duplicates' group and prompt user for resolution.

**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**

Protected term containing a space, such as `{Institutional Author}` trigger the warning "Names are not in the standard biblatex format". Running "Normalize to BibTeX format" does not remove the warning or change the format.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Best: Do not warn. This solution applies to LaTeX and Unicode, and the protected term already displays correctly.

Alternative: Format to `{Institutional\<space>Author}` and remove the warning. This solution applies to LaTeX only.

**Additional context**

Example

```latex
@Article{Last2026-api,
  author       = {Last, F. I. and {Institutional Author}},
  date         = {2026-02-18},
  journaltitle = {Journal of JabRef},
  title        = {Article with a protected institutional author},
}
```
title: Do not warn when author names include protected terms containing space

- [x] I made a backup of my libraries before testing the latest development version.
- [x] I have tested the latest development version and the problem persists

### Steps to reproduce the behaviour

For clean up
1. Go to Quality > Cleanup entries > Single field
2. Add new Field formatter, for example Title:clear
3. Click on Clean up
Result: 0 entry(s) needed a clean up

For save actions
1. Go to Library properties > Saving > Save actions
2. Add new Field formatter, for example Title:clear
3. Click on Apply
4. Save library
Result: library saved, but fields were not cleaned

### Appendix

This problem occurs due to changes made in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/14568.

The button for enabling Field Formatters was removed from `org.jabref.gui.commonfxcontrols.FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel`. Additionally, Field Formatters are now disabled by default in both `org.jabref.logic.cleanup.CleanupPreferences` and `org.jabref.logic.preferences.JabRefCliPreferences`.

While both `org.jabref.gui.cleanup.CleanupSingleFieldPanel` and `org.jabref.gui.libraryproperties.saving.SavingPropertiesView` use FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel, it is currently always disabled with no way to enable it.


#### Proposed Fixes:
1. In CleanupSingleFieldPanel, set FieldFormatterCleanupActions to be always enabled. There is no reason to disable it here; if the user doesn't want to clean up the field, they can simply close the window. https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/d4952b708b5f00d632cc80e174b0cda18a9b3e6b/jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/cleanup/CleanupSingleFieldViewModel.java#L16-L19

2. In SavingPropertiesView, add a button to enable/disable FieldFormatterCleanupActions and store the setting in Metadata.
title: Library save actions and cleanup single field does not work

body:
From JabRef 6.0 onwards, users can apply CSL styles. However, the implementation and features of the old style files and CSL styles are not yet on a par, and, more importantly, they are not interchangeable. 

Until now users may be not aware, that 
1. Writer documents with old-style references do not work with CSL styles.
2. Users cannot switch between the two implementations without getting an incomplete list of references. 

Since references created with CSL or the old style look the same in LO, users may not even be aware of the problem.

**Solution:**
JabRef should make the ReferenceMarks compatible.
Alternatively, the GUI should make users aware of the limitations that arise when using CSL or when switching between the two concepts.

body: ### JabRef version Other (please describe below) 6.0-alpha.403 ### Operating system GNU / Linux ### Details on version and operating system ubuntu:22.04 ### Checked with the [latest development build](https://builds.jabref.org/main/) (copy version output from About dialog) - [x] I made a backup of my libraries before testing the latest development version. - [x] I have tested the latest development version and the problem persists ### Steps to reproduce the behaviour 1. Launch JabRef. 2. Create a new empty library (File → New library). 3. Add one new entry of type Misc. 4. Open the entry editor for the entry and switch to the BibTeX source tab. 5. Replace the source with two BibTeX entries (e.g., an @article and an @book). ``` @article{einstein1905, author = {Einstein, Albert}, title = {Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter K{\"o}rper}, journal = {Annalen der Physik}, year = {1905} } @book{knuth1984, author = {Knuth, Donald E.}, title = {The {\TeX}book}, year = {1984}, publisher = {Addison-Wesley} } ``` 6. Close the entry editor window (this triggers parsing/applying the Source tab). ### Expected Behavior - An error dialog clearly indicates that the failure is caused by the content in the BibTeX/BibLaTeX source tab. - The dialog provides helpful context, such as: - Parsing failed because more than one entry was found. - Guidance like checking the BibTeX syntax. - The dialog title and icon are specific and consistent with a Source tab parsing error, rather than being overly generic. ### Actual Behavior - The dialog title changes from a specific Source-tab-related title (e.g., “Source tab error”) to a generic title (“Error Occurred”). - The dialog icon changes from a warning triangle to a red error cross. - Detailed message and contextual help are removed: - Instead of explaining that the user’s input in the BibTeX source tab caused the failure and showing relevant parsing details, the dialog only shows “More than one entry found.” - An additional blank content area is displayed. ### Screenshot before ### Screenshot after ### Appendix ### Additional examples Move focus to another tab to trigger validation and error handling. **Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**

When I was working on https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/12810, I noticed that it isn't possible to manually enter a keyword containing an escaped delimiter; it works only if I paste the whole keyword.

For example, when I try to create the single keyword "keyword1, keyword2", as soon as I type "keyword1\\,", a new keyword "keyword1\\" is created. If I continue typing "keyword2", I end up with two separate keywords: "keyword1\\" and "keyword2". However, if I paste the string "keyword1\\, keyword2", it behaves as expected and creates a single keyword.

This happens due to logic in org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/KeywordsEditor; 
https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/97d548a2f38e9c5602f330da755c7e06530d161e/jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/KeywordsEditor.java#L124-L130  it checks every symbol that is typed into the field, and if this symbol is a delimiter, it automatically commits the new keyword.

I believe this is confusing for the user and defeats the purpose of the reworked keyword parsing logic.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I have two ideas on how to resolve this issue:

1. Remove the auto-commit logic from KeywordsEditor altogether, so the user must press Enter to create a new keyword.
2. Enhance the logic in KeywordsEditor to check if the separator was escaped before committing the keyword.
title: Allow manual entry of keywords with escaped delimiters

Many researchers publish in journals hosted on Open Journal Systems (OJS). This platform provides an open and free API to track the submissions. It would be handy if researchers cood look at the submissions in JabRef.

Things to implement:

1. Users need a way to add API keys for their OJS journals in the Preferences menu (alongisde the Journal URL).
2. A new option in the Tools menu called "OJS Submission Tracker" should open a dashboard window. This window lists all active submissions across the configured journals with columns for Journal Name, Paper Title, and Status.
3. A new tab should be added to the Entry Editor for OJS tracking. This tab should only be visible if the entry is linked to an OJS submission. It should display the current status of the paper and offer two specific actions:

- Synchronize Metadata: Updates local fields (like Title, DOI, Volume) from the OJS record.
- Download Full Text: Fetches the PDF from OJS and attaches it to the entry.

The feature should rely on the OJS 3.1+ REST API, specifically the `submissions` endpoint.

Technical details:

- The internal OJS `stageId` needs to be mapped to readable statuses (Submission, Peer Review, Copyediting, Production).
- Requests must be authenticated using the Bearer token saved in Preferences.
- To determine visibility of the new entry editor tab, the system should fetch the user's submissions from all configured OJS journals and check if the current entry's title matches any of the retrieved papers.
title: OJS Submission Tracking and Integration

body: 1. Open a library 2. Enable AI - https://docs.jabref.org/ai 3. Attach a PDF 4. Click on "AI Summary" 5. See on the top right corner of JabRef the background task icon 6. Click on it 7. See something similar to\ The text "Waiting summary for ..." should be changed to "Summarizing ..." Development hint: https://devdocs.jabref.org/code-howtos/localization.html
title: Rename "Waiting ..." to "Summarizing ..."

body: 1. Open a library 2. Search in that library 3. Press Ctrl+Shift+F 4. Global search dialog opens\ 5. Press Esc 6. Search is cleared (which is correct) 7. Press Esc (again) Expected: Dialog is closed Actual: Nothing happens Note: If clicking somewhere else in the dialog, it closes on Esc. --- A requriement also needs to be added to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/main/docs/requirements/ux.md - and linked to the implementation. --- Checked 2026-02-16 on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
title: ESC should close the global search dialog

body: Currently, the "Chat with groups" uses a "global" name of the group. If two libraries share the group name, the **wrong** entries might be used. Example Steps to reproduce: 1. Create two libraries 2. Create entries in each library 3. Attach PDF files in each library 4. Enable AI https://docs.jabref.org/ai/preferences 5. Chat with a group 6. Switch to the other library 7. Start chat with a group with the same name See that the chat from step 5 is shown. --- NOTE: This issue shows that the contributor is willing to get familiar with JabRef from the pont of a user.
title: Scope "Chat with groups" to library

body: Follow-up to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/14486 1. Enable AI in JabRef - https://docs.jabref.org/ai/preferences 2. Open a library with a PDF attached - e.g., https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-demonstration-libraries/tree/main/chocolate 3. Select the PDF 4. Go to tab "AI Chat" 5. See that "Export" is enabled\ 6. Expected: The button should only be enabled if there is some chat message This issue requires a diving into JavaFX bindings. --- Also implement if for "Chat with groups"
title: Disable Export button if no AI Chat is there

body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/14486

1. Change back to `this.entries = entries`
2. Check if AI chat export still works.

If yes: file a PR changing back

If not: Report, what breaks.

During the implementation of that fix, I realized that the current user interface for adding fields could be optimized. 
Currently, the distinction or separation between selecting a standard field (via a SearchableComboBox) and entering a custom field name (via a free text field) can be removed.

I have recently revisited this topic and found a way to combine these two inputs into a single control. The solution replaces the separate boxes with a unified TextField that supports auto-completion. This allows users to:
- Select a standard field from the suggestion list
- Type a custom field name freely if it doesn't exist in the list

I have already successfully implemented this solution locally and would appreciate feedback on whether this modification is considered interesting for the project.

Additional context: This is a follow-up to the work done in #14082.

body:
# `METADATA table`

I noticed some aspects of this software that could be improved.

**NOTE**: The following suggestions are not caused by any malfunction.

**Client**:
```
JabRef 5.15--2024-07-10--1eb3493
Windows 10 10.0 amd64 
Java 21.0.2 
JavaFX 22.0.1+7
```

Server:
```
PostgreSQL 13.22 (Raspbian 13.22-0+deb11u1) on Raspbian 10.2.1-6+rpi1, 32-bit
```


## Current `METADATA table`

```mermaid
erDiagram
METADATA {
        string KEY
        string VALUE
    }
```

1. `METADATA table` **haven't a PRIMARY KEY**
2. Fields `KEY`, `VALUES` **aren't homogeneous**,
    there are:
    - *fileDirectoryLatex* (**user**+**machine**): they can to be more than 1.
    - *VersionDBStructure*: versione DB Structure
    - *databaseType*: bib
    - *grouping*: similar to table

## Suggestions `fileDirectoryLatex ---> ConfigUsers`

From pair **`KEY+VALUE`** to **Table `ConfigUsers`**

```mermaid
erDiagram
ConfigUsers {
        string machine PK
        string user PK
        string path_folder
    }
```

## Current `grouping` (pair KEY+VALUE)

In this database version *grouping* (pair KEY+VALUE) **must be unique**, and represents **hierarchical data**.

*grouping* defines lateral menu in JabRef.

*grouping* currently looks like this:

```mermaid
erDiagram
grouping {
        integer Level
        string Type
        string Item_name
        integer Hierarchical_context
        string criteria
        string Keyword_Delimiter_**OR**_case_sensitive
        string Hierarchical_Keyword_Delimiter_**OR**_regular_expression
        integer unknown
        string Color
        string Icon
        string Description
    }
```

Attributes that define *class group* are two:

- **Level** defines hierarchy but without reference to its parent or children (Hierarchical and positional system)
- **Type** defines typology of group with own properties:
  - AllEntriesGroup
  - AutomaticPersonsGroup
  - AutomaticKeywordGroup
  - StaticGroup
  - Other

I found an ambiguity in columns 6 and 7, because conceptually different data is stored in them:

- **Culumn 6**: Keyword_Delimiter **OR** case_sensitive
- **Culumn 7**: Hierarchical_Keyword_Delimiter **OR** regular_expression

## Suggestions `grouping`

*grouping* represents hierarchical data or nested data, so why don't we use **json type**?

- Not all databases handle json the same way, but Java can.
- Today there is a requirement to have only one hierarchical menu, in the near future it may be necessary to leave each user the possibility to create their own grouping.
  - we could embed the key into the table `ConfigUsers`

```mermaid
erDiagram
ConfigUsers {
        string machine PK
        string user PK
        string path_folder
        json grouping
    }
```

An example of structure json:

```json
{
  "groups": [
    {
      "type": "AllEntriesGroup",
      "name": "AllEntries",
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "AutomaticPersonsGroup",
          "name": "By Author",
          "field": "author",
          "color": "0x800080ff",
          "icon": "ACCOUNT",
          "children": []
        },
        {
          "type": "AutomaticKeywordGroup",
          "name": "By Keywords",
          "field": "keywords",
          "color": "0x800080ff",
          "icon": "KEY_VARIANT",
          "children": []
        },
        {
          "type": "StaticGroup",
          "name": "Categories",
          "color": "0x800080ff",
          "icon": "FOLDER_MULTIPLE_PLUS",
          "children": [
            {
              "type": "StaticGroup",
              "name": "Article",
              "color": "0xff00ffff",
              "icon": "ACCOUNT_ALERT"
            },
            {
              "type": "SearchGroup",
              "name": "Book",
              "field": "book",
              "color": "0xd329c8ff",
              "icon": "FOLDER_MULTIPLE_PLUS"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Hierarchical menu

[Jabref Group - Menu](https://docs.jabref.org/finding-sorting-and-cleaning-entries/groups)

Json in databases:

- [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/json1.html)
- [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions-json.html)
- [MariaDB](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/reference/sql-functions/special-functions/json-functions)
- [Oracle DB](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/21/adjsn/json-in-oracle-database.html)
title: METADATA Table - Structure Update with JSON

<!--
Please use the GitHub issue tracker only for bug reports and smaller suggestions for improvements.
Requests for completely new features, questions and general feedback is now handled at https://discourse.jabref.org.
Thanks!
-->

**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**
Yes. I've identified a "Long Method" code smell in `org.jabref.logic.importer.util.FileFieldParser.java`.

The `parse()` method is overly complex and handles several distinct logical concerns within a single loop: checking for empty values, handling online links, and managing a character-by-character parsing state machine with multiple flags (like `xmlChar`, `escaped`, `windowsPath`). This makes the code difficult to read and maintain.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I propose to refactor the `parse()` method using the "Extract Method" technique.

I plan to break down the complex logic into smaller, well-named private helper methods. The goal is to make the main `parse()` method act as a high-level coordinator. This will significantly improve readability and make the parsing logic easier to maintain and test.

**Additional context**
I am a student in Ellen Spertus's class working on a code quality assignment. I identified this opportunity for improvement and would like to contribute the refactoring via a PR. @espertusnu
title: Refactor: Improve FileFieldParser parsing logic

I just tried the version 6.0 alpha 3 since I wanted to benefit from the support of CSL styles for LibreOffice.
My publisher request APA 7...

But I am also using citekeys within the XML documents produced by another piece of software (Scrivener) and I was thus so far relying on the nice little LibreOffice plugin **JabRef_LibreOffice_Converter** from @teertinker which allows to turn `\cite{citationkey}` in the XML document opened in LibreOffice into an active citation that JabRef understands.

With version JabRef 6.0, this no longer works (the active citations created by the plugin are not recognised by JabRef).
Perhaps this is just some glitch connected to the alpha stage of 6.0, or perhaps there is something to change in **JabRef_LibreOffice_Converter**.

In any case, I wanted to flag this possibly new incompatibility.
title: Version 6.0 no longer works with JabRef_LibreOffice_Converter

body: Currently, the `generate-citation-keys` command from JabKit doesn't allow for customization ``` Usage: jabkit generate-citation-keys [-dhp] --input= [--output=] Generate citation keys for entries in a .bib file. -d, --debug Enable debug output -h, --help display this help message --input= Input BibTeX file --output= The output .bib file. -p, --porcelain Enable script-friendly output ``` However, JabRef allows for much customization: https://docs.jabref.org/setup/citationkeypatterns This should also be offered in the CLI. You can check the GUI for the options Task: - Offer each element of `CitationKeyPatternPreferences` as parameter in the CLI for `org.jabref.toolkit.commands.GenerateCitationKeys` - Thereby, construct new `org.jabref.logic.citationkeypattern.CitationKeyPatternPreferences` based on CLI options. If no option is provided for a parameter, use the values from user-configured `JabRefCliPreferences` (argumentProcessor.cliPreferences). Hints: - You can use org.jabref.toolkit.converter.CaseInsensitiveEnumConverter to convert an enum (see usage of the class for how to do) - Key patterns is a map, which can be implemented in PicoCLI using https://picocli.info/#_maps
title: Enable parameters for CLI: generate-citation-keys

body:
It looks like the imports
https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/main/jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/UnpaywallFetcher.java#L20
in line 20 and 21 have not been adjusted to Jackson 3.

This makes Jackson 2 an unexpected dependency.  I don't know how this could pass tests, but in my (non-gradle) build I get the issue
```
.../src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/UnpaywallFetcher.java:20: error: package com.fasterxml.jackson.databind is not visible
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
                            ^
  (package com.fasterxml.jackson.databind is declared in module com.fasterxml.jackson.databind, but module org.jabref.jablib does not read it)
```
and a similar one for `ObjectMapper`.
I assume by some magic trick gradle's automatic resolution somehow circumvents this issue. Still, it should be fixed. All that needs to be done is replace
```java
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
```
by
```java
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
```
in `UnpaywallFetcher.java`.
title: Move to Jackson 3: forgotten imports in UnpaywallFetcher can cause issue

body:
Several utility classes in the codebase contain only static methods but lack both the `final` modifier and a private constructor to prevent instantiation and subclassing. This violates Java best practices for utility classes and could lead to misuse.

Add the `final` modifier to each utility class declaration and include a private constructor that throws `UnsupportedOperationException` to explicitly prevent instantiation. This follows the standard pattern recommended in "Effective Java" by Joshua Bloch.

**Affected classes:**
1. `org.jabref.logic.icore.ConferenceUtils`
2. `org.jabref.logic.ai.util.CitationKeyCheck`
3. `org.jabref.logic.importer.util.StaxParser`
4. `org.jabref.logic.importer.util.JsonReader`
5. `org.jabref.logic.importer.util.MathMLParser`
6. `org.jabref.logic.git.merge.planning.util.ConflictRules`

This refactoring has no behavioral changes and improves code quality by making the intent of these utility classes explicit. Each class will be addressed in a separate pull request for easier review.

This was discussed and approved on Gitter by @koppor .
title: Code Refactoring

**The suggestion for improvement is related to the following problem**
I want to filter entries to a certain date ranges

E.g. JabRef should provide me with a list of all documents in my library that were published between 2001-05-17 and 2009-02-18.


**Any of the below solutions would suffice**
- [ ] Add this feature to the search bar
- [ ] Add this feature to group by date

**Additional context**
refs https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/8902
refs https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/14241, https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/14169
[ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)
According to https://docs.jabref.org/finding-sorting-and-cleaning-entries/search#searching-with-optional-spelling we already could do this with regex: 
`year == 200[5-9]|201[0-1]​specifies the range of years 2005-2011 (200[5-9] specifies years 2005-2009;| means "or"; 201[0-1] specifies years 2010-2011).`
But I want something easier. Something that doesn't force me to type hundreds or lines of search expressions, if the date range is across multiple decades.
title: Filter entries down to certain date ranges

body:
This issue has multiple areas of exploration, not recommended for newcomers but highly recommended for people who love debugging.

Chronological navigation per-library was re-introduced in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/13863

## Phase 1 - Experiments
The following cases were not taken into consideration during development:
1. What happens if multiple entries are selected (using Ctrl + click), and then another entry/group of entries are selected? - Investigate. See if you are able to co-relate the behavior with the code.
2. What happens if an entry that is present in the navigation history is deleted (removed from the library), and then one tries to navigate to it chronologically? - Investigate. (https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/17353)
3. [done] https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13878 (most probably an issue with listeners)

## Phase 2 - Development
### Plan & hints
- In case of 1, we should support selecting a group of entries as one history "entity" that we can chronologically traverse back and forth to. Motivation behind this idea can be found in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/13863#issuecomment-3335225687 (cc: @InAnYan). One obvious idea may be using a "list of list of history entries" per library instead of a "list of history entries". Challenge would be to demarcate the previous group of entries from the next group and adding it to the next list inside the parent list. A hint can be to find if existing methods/listeners (or new ones, if needed) can be used to trace the "de-selection of previous selected entries due to selection of a new one" - and this "new one" can be an entry belonging inside or outside the previously selected group. In simpler words (from a user's perspective), imagine ctrl+clicking a couple of entries, then "just" clicking on any entry - so that the previous ones are de-selected. 
- For part 1, another aspect to take care of would be "which entry should be displayed in the entry editor if a group of entries is navigated to in history?" - A simple answer to this would be the standard expected behavior - when normally selecting a group (using ctrl+ clicks), the last entry selected is the one open in the entry editor. So during chronological navigation too, the last selected entry of the group (in order of addition in the sub-list mentioned above) before the next group (list) is introduced should be the correct state to restore for "undo"/"redo" to open in the entry editor. Lets call this an "anchor" entry. This anchor entry for each group (sub-list) should be separately marked/captured so that at the end of the navigation action, it can be selected in the entry editor.
- In case of 2, if any unexpected behavior occurs, report it under this issue and improve the implementation to handle it gracefully - removed entries should also be removed from the navigation history. Navigation should work as intended - as if the removed entries never existed during the creation of the history list. If the behavior is already fine, report that too. (This may also intertwined with point 1)
- In case of 3, details of what to do are already given in the linked issue.

> [!NOTE]
> Since this is a **user-facing** change, a **screen recording** of the functionality working in JabRef UI is **mandatory** to be provided in the description of the PR to mark completion.
title: Improve chronological navigation

body:
**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**
The `importDatabase()` method in [OvidImporter](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/main/jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/OvidImporter.java) has grown into a long method that mixes multiple functionalities including record splitting, per-field parsing, regex handling for Source fields, and final cleanup. This makes it harder to understand, test, and maintain.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I’d like to refactor `importDatabase()` by extracting several small private helper methods (`parseSource()`, `parseField()`, `normalizeContributors()`, and `resolveEntryType()`) while preserving all current behavior and public APIs. The goal is purely to improve readability and separation of concerns, not to change functionality.

**Additional context**
This refactoring proposal was discussed and approved on the JabRef Gitter channel.

Would you prefer helper methods like these to be annotated with `@VisibleForTesting` and have direct unit tests, or should testing rely solely on the existing integration-level coverage for `OvidImporter`? I understand there are different schools of thought on this and would like to follow JabRef’s convention.
title: Refactor long method importDatabase() in OvidImporter

body:
Our pseudonymization mechanism in [`org.jabref.logic.pseudonymization.Pseudonymization`](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/main/jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/pseudonymization/Pseudonymization.java) is not exhaustive - for instance, it misses the pseudonymization of [groups](https://docs.jabref.org/finding-sorting-and-cleaning-entries/groups).
The goal is to add that.


**Additional context**
- JabRef groups: https://docs.jabref.org/finding-sorting-and-cleaning-entries/groups
- The information about groups is contained in the `.bib` file itself, at the bottom, with `@Comment`.
- One can explore the above using [Chocolate.bib](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/main/jablib/src/main/resources/Chocolate.bib) and co-relate with what is happening in the GUI (groups section, and also by adding new groups).
- The entry point to use pseudonymization is currently under JabKit (CLI), with hints to use in [this](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/13158) PR that added it.
- Use JabRef's classes to interact with groups (this also updates `@Comment` content)
- Remember that `groups` field has **multiple** groups - and the names are the links into the groups tree.

> [!NOTE]
> A **screen recording** in the description of the PR of this functionality working is **mandatory** for marking completion. That is, the output bib file and the pseudonymized groups should be visible in the recording.
title: Pseudonymize groups

**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**
Some classes use `String.replaceAll()` with inline regex patterns, rather than pre-compiling them as `static final Pattern` fields following [Java regex best practices](https://www.baeldung.com/java-regex-pre-compile).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Pre-compile regex patterns as `private static final Pattern` fields at the class level, following the approach already used in classes such as `LatexCleanupFormatter` and `BibliographyFromPdfImporter`.

I originally identified this pattern in `EuropePmcFetcher` (date validation pattern `"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}"`), but found similar patterns in other files:
- [ ] `EuropePmcFetcher` - date validation pattern
- [ ] `BstPreviewLayout` -  in `generatePreview()`
- [ ] `HtmlToUnicodeFormatter` - HTML tag removal pattern
- [ ] `JstorFetcher` - URL query pattern


**Additional context**
I posted about the initial `EuropePmcFetcher` change on Gitter and Christoph said it was a positive change. Would you prefer one PR for `EuropePmcFetcher` or could I address the regex pre-compiling in the other files listed as well?

body: In science, authors write papers. They related their paper to other papers. This text is very interesting, as it contains two aspects: - interesting other papers - description of other papers Example: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-demo-libraries/blob/main/chocolate/pdfs/LunaOstos_2024%20-%20Social%20Life%20Cycle%20Assessment%20in%20the%20Chocolate%20Industry%20-%20A%20Colombian%20Case%20Study%20with%20Luker%20Chocolate.pdf ``` Colombia is a middle-income country with a population of approximately 50 million (CIA 2021), with at least 11 million people living in rural areas (DANE 2018). It is the third most biodiverse country globally, following Brazil and Indonesia (Nash 2022). ``` JabRef should do following: For each reference: - Lookup in the references - Add to library - or update, if already exists - Find out descriptive text for the paper in the text - Add the desriptive text to `comments-{username}`, prefixed with `[{citation-key}]: ` (`[LunaOstos_2024] ` in our example). In case there is already content in `comments-{username}`, just append it. Separated by an empty line. Example result: ```bibtex @Misc{Agency2021, author = {{Central Intelligence Agency}}, note = {Accessed 4 Mar 2023}, title = {The world factbook: Colombia}, year = {2021}, comment-koppor = {[LunaOstos_2024]: Colombia is a middle-income country with a population of approximately 50 million.}, url = {https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/colombia/}, } ``` --- ## UI Add a new tab "Related work text" When pasting here, it is parsed and entries created / updated accordingly --- Related: Citation relations. However, they do not have the full text. Screenshot from the linked PDF: Fuller context: --- Hint: It is perfectly OK to use the langchain4j's AI interface to parse etc. --- This is NOT citation relations, because this issue here is about to harvest knowledge from a PDF. --- **This requires Software Engineering** not simply generating a wall of code. As a consequence, you need to split into parts. One step by one step. Do a new PR. One step after another. With UML diagrams and documentation. No rush. We need to be more close to the initial requirement. First PR: Setting - User has opened an IEEE paper in their PDF reader. E.g., the one at https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/15069. - User has selected the respective BibEntry in JabRef 1. User selects reference text in their PDF reader 2. User copies text to clipboard 3. User selects "Tools" -> "Insert related work text" 4. JabRef opens dialog with current clipboard content 5. Dialog shows if the reference is matched in the the current library - if not, JabRef offers to add the reference. This is a s sub-paert of the dialog. 6. User clicks "Insert" (only enabled if the reference is found in the bib file) 7. JabRef adds the reference to the linked reference as "- {citationkey}: {text}" 8. JabRef displays notification "reference summary added" 9. JabRef closes dialog Note: The reference text need to be added as item at a markdown list. This eases separating references. You can even split up the PR more and first work on the logic part. Maybe even - "only" extracting text + reference "text" --> correct data structures and tests. Example: `A study on the Colombian [...] [1].` - finds `A study on the Colombian [...]` and `[1]` - Finding the reference "text" in the references section. E.g., `[1]` is turned into a "pointer" to BibEntry `LunaOstos_2024` Then the UI part Then continue at reference format `[1, 2]` - separate PR Then use one (!) other reference format. Create a test PDF for that. Then work on another reference format. Create a test PDF for that. Then support for multiple references, e.g., ```markdown A study on the Colombian chocolate industry represents the first application of a social life cycle assessment (S-LCA) to cover both cocoa cultivation and chocolate manufacturing [1]. A study on selective, hedonic deprivation found that restricting chocolate intake for two weeks increased state chocolate crav- ing, but only in individuals who already had high trait choco- late craving [2]. ```
title: Extract text about papers from "related work" sections

**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**

There are places where BibEntry could be improved:

1. The semantics of the `withX()` methods are unclear. Specifically
     * Should it be called immediately after construction and before use?
     * Should it return `this` or a new instance?
2. There are methods that return mutable fields but do not create defensive copies.
3. There is code that is uncalled, including from tests. I spotted a bug in [one of these methods](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/ca3821a68e4eef7b4e79a12313c46672734e171d/jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntry.java#L917).
4. [getSourceField()](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/ca3821a68e4eef7b4e79a12313c46672734e171d/jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntry.java#L191) could be rewritten in a (slightly) more data-driven manner, with, for example, lists of forbidden fields rather than multi-way disjunctions.
5. `@NotNull` keyword could be added.
 
**Describe the solution you'd like**

I would like clarifications on the desired semantics and for this issue to be assigned to me and my students.

**Additional context**

I am an instructor looking for an exercise for my students.

@koppor said on Gitter:

> We have `BibEntry#withField` and more "withers". However, they modify the Object at hand - and thus contradict the expection of a "wither" to create a copy. All of these could be rewritten to be a proper builder.
title: Improve BibEntry

body:
**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**

I observe at least one package and even class name collision between two JabRef Modules:

`org.jabref.cli.ArgumentProcessor` exists in jabgui and jabkit and both classes are quite different. They have completely different members, so this is more than just a shadowing hack.
While technically possible, already the package name clash is bad style. So-called split packages are discouraged in the Java module system and can cause unforeseen issues.

From https://dev.java/learn/modules/intro/:

> Packages should have a unique origin, so no two modules can contain types in the same package. If they do, this is called a split package, and the module system will refuse to compile or launch such configurations.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Please refactor to avoid split packages as it is an unnecessary risk and source of trouble. The earlier this is done, the easier the change will be. I strongly recommend to adjust this before beta phase.
title: Package and Class name collision accross modules

During JabCon 2025, we worked on adding some new features and possibly breaking changes. One of these included "[Chronological navigation in libraries](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/13863)". 
This was essentially an improved "per-tab" version of the same feature which [existed in JabRef 4.x](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/6352) and was removed in 5.x

### Steps to reproduce the behaviour

1. Open JabRef
2. Open an empty library

5. See that the navigation buttons are available, and sometimes some sequence of pressing them can take you to certain entries

## Possible hint to solution
When any new entry is added/imported, the maintable selects it via:

to show which entry was last added.
In case of bulk imports, there is no defined order of import (and thus no defined order of selections), and these selections should not be counted in the navigation history.
The challenge will be to track when bulk imports happen and disable the history list updates in such cases.

body: **Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.** Quite often, JabRef users would like to share a conversation with AI, or store it in some text file that would be read later without opening JabRef. However, currently we don't have an option of saving the conversation or summary to some external file. **Describe the solution you'd like** Add a button to chat and summary tab that allows user to export a summary or a chat to a file. That should give a dropdown: - `Export in human-readable format (Markdown)` - `Export in machine-readable format (JSON)` I got this idea from Telegram messenger, where there are also 2 options for exporting chats. Exporting in machine-readable format could be useful for other AI tools or knowledge bases. After clicking on one of the buttons, an file dialog should open. **Additional context** Format for **human-readable option** (`<` and `>` denote special places in text that needs to be replaced): ```markdown ## Bibtex \`\`\`bibtex \`\`\` ## Conversation **User:** Format to store chats with ai in Markdown? **AI:** A common and clean way... ``` *`\` should not be added, I added them because there are nested backticks in this issue description*. Format for **machine-readable option**: ```json { "entry_bibtex": "", "entry": {"": "", "": "" }, "latest_provider": "", "latest_model": "", "timestamp": ", "conversation": [ {"role": "user", "content": "<...>"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "<...>"} ] } ``` Notes on machine-readable format: - `conversation` should follow [OpenAI API format](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/conversation-state?api-mode=chat). - We paste `entry` in dictionary form because some programs would like to use this as metadata naturally without parsing bibtex. - I added `latest_` prefixes, because the model is not saved in the data model of a conversation, and it only depends on current JabRef preferences. - Timestampt is not available for chats. - However, summaries have recorded chat model, provider, and timestamp, which you can use
title: Add export chat and summary feature to AI functionality

**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**

The field of AI/LLM is constantly improving, more and more models are available now. However, specific LLM models are hardcoded in JabRef, and maintainers sometimes don't have time to properly update everything. In any case, manual resolution and hardcoded values smells.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Implement any automatic way of determining the latest LLM models into JabRef, so that maintainers and users don't have to update anything.

**Additional context**

This is an _engineering_ task, as, at the moment of writing this issue, I don't have any concrete ideas to implement. A contributor should research the ways on their own
title: Automatically determine latest language models

(This is a follow-up to #13584)

We have a library consistency check for checking whether fields in a set of entries are set/unset consistently. Currently, this is aware of the difference of BibTeX and BibLaTeX, but not [Custom Entry Types](https://docs.jabref.org/setup/customentrytypes) 

⚠ This is a good excercise to learn test-driven development and using a data model. This issue cannot be solved with an AI. You really have to think though BibTeX and BibLaTeX for yourself! Take this issue only if you are willing to invest significant time. ⚠

Example entry - from https://dblp.org/rec/journals/sqj/IftikharBAK25.html

```bibtex
@article{DBLP:journals/sqj/IftikharBAK25,
  author       = {Umar Iftikhar and
                  J{\"{u}}rgen B{\"{o}}rstler and
                  Nauman Bin Ali and
                  Oliver Kopp},
  title        = {Supporting the identification of prevalent quality issues in code
                  changes by analyzing reviewers' feedback},
  journal      = {Softw. Qual. J.},
  volume       = {33},
  number       = {2},
  pages        = {22},
  year         = {2025},
  url          = {https://doi.org/10.1007/s11219-025-09720-9},
  doi          = {10.1007/S11219-025-09720-9},
  timestamp    = {Mon, 12 May 2025 21:02:32 +0200},
  biburl       = {https://dblp.org/rec/journals/sqj/IftikharBAK25.bib},
  bibsource    = {dblp computer science bibliography, https://dblp.org}
}
```

It contains `bibourl` and `bibsource`

One could make these two fields required.

```bibtex
@article{withBibSource,
  journal      = {Softw. Qual. J.},
  bibsource = {2025}
}

@article{withoutBibSource,
  journal      = {Softw. Qual. J.},
}
```

With the existing consistency check, `bibsource` is reported as `unknown`. If the entry type `article` is modified to have this as optional field, it is reported as optional.

## Task

- Modify `org.jabref.logic.quality.consistency.BibliographyConsistencyCheck` to use `org.jabref.model.entry.BibEntryTypesManager` instead of org.jabref.model.entry.types.BiblatexEntryTypeDefinitions#ALL

## Hints

- Do test-driven development. Start at`org.jabref.logic.quality.consistency.BibliographyConsistencyCheckTest`. Do not modify existing tests; add new ones.
- Look into `org.jabref.model.entry.BibEntryTypesManagerTest` for how to mock `BibEntryTypesManager`.
- Do not get confused with "library" and "database". User-facing we talk about "library", inside the code, we use "database", but mean "library".
title: Support customized entry types in BibliographyConsistencyCheck

JabRef allows for fixing field content. Example: Use only one space instead of multiple ones in a field. These is called "formatters" in JabRef. 

Example: org.jabref.logic.formatter.bibtexfields.NormalizeWhitespaceFormatter

The class `org.jabref.logic.cleanup.ISSNCleanup` is such a formatter, but its implemetned as Cleanup. Which is wrong. --> CleanUps are used for multi-field operations.

Task

1. Move `org.jabref.logic.cleanup.ISSNCleanup` to package `org.jabref.logic.formatter.bibtexfields`
2. Rename to `NormalizeIssn`
3. Make it `extends Formatter` (remove `implements CleanupJob`)
4. Adapt code accordingly
  - Remove from "Miscallenous" section in cleanup dialog
  - Add the formatter to `org.jabref.logic.cleanup.FieldFormatterCleanups#DEFAULT_SAVE_ACTIONS` (only for field `org.jabref.model.entry.field.StandardField#ISSN`)

Micro task:

Fix formatting in `jabgui/src/main/resources/org/jabref/gui/cleanup/CleanupPresetPanel.fxml` - the indent is wrong. (from line 48 on)

---

This is a follow-up to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/1590.
title: Make `ISSNCleanup` a `Formatter`

Misses `check-integrity`. Needs to be added.
